result.description:
About the Client:  
Our client is more than just a team of professionals; they treat their team members as part of the family, ensuring they are respected, heard, and supported. 
 
They are dedicated to delivering exceptional services and, by joining them, you'll become part of a dynamic, passionate team focused on empowering individuals to reach their full potential. Their organization plays a vital role in improving the lives of those with disabilities and challenges related to learning and behavior, with the team leading the way in shaping the future of allied health support. If you share their values, they would be delighted to have you on board. 
 
 Responsibilities:  

 
	 Day to day overseeing a leading and innovative team. 
	 Apply and extend your extensive clinical knowledge through professional development with staff, 
	 Ensure high level professionalism and ethical conduct, 
	 Partner with clients throughout their therapy journey, our stepped-out pathway to exceptional outcomes. 
	 allied health assistants. 
	 Utilise the next generation of client management systems 
	 And much more to ensure a successful and rewarding team, clinic and clients. 
 

  
 About You:  

 
	 You are naturally driven! A person who thrives on seeing others succeed. 
	 Approachable and empathetic towards those we assist. 
	 Naturally, you have a love for working with children.  You will have extensive experience working in early intervention in either private or public. 
	 You have grown over the years in your clinical experience and are perhaps currently working as an OT / Senior OT who is wanting to take the next step into a Team Leader role whilst still drawing on your clinical experience. 
	 Must be an excellent communicator with the ability to engage with our community. 
	 You love what you do, and this shows in your ability to engage and build relationships. 
	 Above all, you are ready to take on this opportunity and grow as a leader in your field. 
	 Hold academic qualifications together with professional registration (AHPRA). 
	 Lastly, you are enthusiastic and willing to jump in and hit the ground running! 
 

  
 What's on Offer:  

 
	 Join a fantastic team of professionals in an inclusive environment, working with a diverse range of clients and services. 
	 Enjoy an attractive remuneration package. 
	 Benefit from a strong focus on ongoing training and development, 
	 Work across various areas, including assessments and more. 
	 Receive comprehensive administrative support and additional benefits. 
          Apply Now

Department for Health and Wellbeing - Workforce Services - Strategic Industrial Relations and Policy 

Salary: $139,538 - SM1 - Full Time - Ongoing - Permanent 

Overview:

The Manager Strategy and Projects reports to the Director, Strategic Industrial Relations and Policy and provides senior management leadership and authoritative specialist expertise in the development and delivery of complex, system-wide multi-functional and multi-disciplinary workforce and industrial relations strategies, policies and programs of critical strategic importance, and workplace change.

The role operates with a high degree of professional autonomy and judgement and provides authoritative advice that directly informs and influences strategy, policy, planning and executive decision-making across SA Health.

The key outcomes for this role include:

Develop and lead system-wide workforce relations strategies that drive long-term organisational and system-wide transformation, underpinned by research, analysis, and innovation.

Develop and lead the implementation of system-wide workforce relations policies and frameworks, in collaboration with key senior stakeholders across the SA Health network.

Lead the development, integration and governance of consolidated Enterprise Bargaining (EB) forward plans as part of short, medium, and long-term strategic industrial relations plans and their implementation. 

Proactively identify strategic opportunities to drive organisational and system-wide transformation through workplace relations reform, including the development of pathways for implementation across the system.

Provide strategic leadership and oversight of highly complex, multi-disciplinary and multi-functional programs and initiatives, where outcomes have critical system-wide and cross-agency impact.

Lead the review, redesign and implementation of system-wide workplace relations policies and procedures to enable new ways of working, strategic objectives, and Service Level Agreements.

Support the delivery of objectives and priorities as set by Health Chief Executive Council (HCEC) and form strong working relationships with HCEC.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment)
